title: Hourly improvements
items: One-tap instant offer: every mic/outboard deal push now has an "Offer $X" button and the deal emails an Offer link. It opens a phone-friendly /offer page with the ask, used value, a suggested offer (about 15% under, never under 70% of the ask, rounded to $5, shipped to Seattle), an editable amount, and one Send button (Reverb/eBay offers, with the usual confirm, logged in the offer log) or a Copy message button for other sites. Home cards with a suggested offer show the same "Offer $X" link.
Rare find chip: listings of rare/vintage models (Neumann U47, AKG C12, Telefunken ELA M 251, Pultec, Fairchild and similar) get a purple "Rare find" tag on the card, whatever the price.
Price per channel: multi-channel preamps and interfaces (like an 8-channel preamp) now show "$X per channel" on the card, in green when it's $75 or less per channel.

Outboard page: lists current 1176, LA-2A, Fairchild, EQP-1A/Pultec, API/CAPI 500 module, Distressor, WA-412, Neve and Neumann/Telex preamps and compressors asking 20%+ under their used value, newest and biggest discount first (very big discounts are marked double-check).
Price-range dimmer: mic cards priced far outside what you usually star appear dimmed (never hidden) on Home and Mics; starred ads and real deals are never dimmed.
Home, Mics and the other lists now hide vinyl-record and non-gear ads that were stored before the junk guard existed (the Ronco Records album was still showing).
Best month to buy: under a mic model's price chart on the Mics page, a line like "Cheapest month to buy: June (about 18% under average)" appears when there's at least a year of ads to back it up.
Catch speed: the Sources page has a new card showing, for each site, how many minutes after an ad is posted Gear Scout typically finds it (Facebook times are rough).
Starred-ad nudge: if an ad you starred is still for sale a day later, you get one gentle push ("Still thinking about this one? It's still up at $X"), at most twice a day and only in daytime.
Shopping-list deals: a brand-new listing for something on your studio shopping list that is 25%+ under its usual price now sends a push (items with your own price target keep using that target).
Vinyl records, CDs and cassettes whose titles happen to hold a mic model number (like the Ronco Records "RE-1000" album) no longer show up as gear.

title: Code review
items: Home: a "reposted N×" tag could stick to an ad on other pages where the copies weren't folded together. It now only shows on the folded card.

title: Hourly improvements
items: Send offer on eBay: on eBay Buy It Now cards that take Best Offer, a button sends your suggested offer from your own eBay account (asks to confirm first, shows eBay's real reason if it fails). Connect your eBay account once under Settings > eBay; the click-by-click steps are in docs/ebay_connect_steps.md.
Offer log: tap "Log an offer" on any card to record what you offered and the reply; the new Offers page shows which discounts and sellers actually work.
Price history: /mics now charts each model's asking price over time, with a Buy now / Wait / Steady badge.
Seller watchlist: tap "Watch seller" on a card and you get a push whenever that seller posts something new; see them on the Sellers page.
Regional price gap: /mics flags models that are 25%+ cheaper in another state than at home, with links to the cheapest ads.
Fast lane now also watches Reverb compressors and preamps (Distressor, LA-2A, 1176, Fairchild, API/CAPI); Reverb cards and pushes show an "Offers OK" tag with your usual offer.
HiBid auctions are now a source, checked with the same used-value rules (Proxibid and GovDeals block scrapers, so they were skipped).
Motivated sellers: ads saying moving, closing, estate, divorce or must sell get a tag, a deeper suggested offer, and a Home section.
Flips: new page of cheap listings you could resell on Reverb at a profit, with a draft listing and a profit tracker. It posts nothing.
Resale profit: deal cards now show "Resell ~$X profit", what the mic should net on Reverb after fees and shipping, when that is $50 or more.
Missing accessories: ads for mics that normally come with a shock mount or case, but never mention one, get a "No shock mount / case?" tag.

Bundle breakdown: when an ad sells several things together (mic + preamp + cables), Gear Scout adds up the used value of each piece and tags the card "Bundle: $X vs ~$Y of parts" if the ask is 40%+ under.
Quiet auctions: new Home section listing eBay mic auctions ending within 6 hours with zero bids and a price 40%+ under used value, soonest first.
Stubborn-seller flag: ads whose price has been cut 2 or more times get a "Cut 2x — motivated" tag, a good sign to lowball.
Room to haggle: ads that say OBO, "make offer" or "must sell" get a tag, and the offer helper opens about 20% lower on them.
Sunday buyer's report: every Sunday at 8:30 AM you get one email with the week's new mics, price drops, what sold and a market headline.
Price history: ads whose price has changed now show a tiny line chart next to the price (green = cheaper, red = pricier). Hover or long-press to see each price.
Sold-out alert: when a listing you starred sells or is taken down, you get one push and email (only for ones that sold in the last 2 days).
Price targets: new panel on the Mics page. Type a model and the most you'd pay; you get a push the moment any ad for it, deal or not, is at or under that price.
Offer helper: every mic deal now shows a suggested opening offer (about 10% under asking) and a walk-away price, with a Copy message button. Before, only price-dropped or long-listed ads got one.

Send offer on Reverb: Reverb deal cards with a suggested offer get a "Send offer on Reverb" button. It asks you to confirm in the page, then sends only on your second tap and logs it in the Offer log. If Reverb refuses, you see its reason and a message to copy. Reverb doesn't publish the offer fields, so the first real send may need a tweak.

title: Nightly improvements
items: New Shopping list page (in the menu next to Telex List): your cable and connector list from the Rev H wiring plan, each item matched to the 3 cheapest ads that are still for sale, with an estimated price including WA tax and shipping, and the price of buying new for comparison.
At the top: what's still to buy in total, an optional budget box (it tells you if you're over or under), and a Bought tick for each item so it drops out of the total.
Feed: car-audio ads (MB Quart amps, "SSL Force" subwoofers) no longer match your "ssl" search.
Look at: some items have no used ad yet (5 of 28 had a match tonight), so they're priced as new. A few matches can be bundles, so open the ad before you buy.

title: Nightly check
items: Health check: all Wanted terms searched in the last 20 minutes on quick sites and eBay; new ads reach you in a median 2.2 h (7 of 16 within an hour); 197 of the top 200 Feed ads were re-checked for sold in the last 6 hours.
Facebook: many Wanted terms still show 11 days since their last search because Mic Focus was on until Nov 1; the rotation is catching up at the same Facebook load.
No errors in either container in the last 24 hours. No code change tonight.
New idea added to Coming next: Offer helper (suggested opening offer and walk-away price on each deal). Studio shopping list is still approved and queued for the hourly builder.

title: Hourly improvements
items: Mics page has a new "Market pulse" panel: for each mic brand, new ads per week, the typical asking price per week, and how fast they usually sell. The up/down arrow only appears once there's enough history to trust it.
Mic deal pushes now end with how long similar mics usually take to sell (e.g. "similar mics usually sell in ~4 days"), so you know how fast to move.

Mic Focus is off: Gear Scout searches your whole Telex List again, with the mic searches in the same rotation (every search gets the same check rate, least recently searched first). Home is now new results plus 'Smokin' hot deals' (Telex List and mic deals together, best score first), then a small Distressor section (it's a compressor, not a mic, so it's no longer under Mics), a collapsed Mics section with the lowest price per model, Coming next, and Check these. The full menu is back with Home first. The 2-minute fast lane now always runs, so hot mic deals still push right away, with the same deal rules. You can turn Mic Focus back on from the Mics page.

Fast lane for fresh mics: every 2 minutes Gear Scout now checks only the newest Reverb and eBay Buy It Now mic listings, and a mic that meets your usual deal rules is pushed within a couple of minutes of being posted instead of waiting for the next 15-minute round. Same rules and prices as before; nothing is pushed twice.
Telex page has a new "Sharper terms" box: for broad searches like 'ssl' or 'drawmer' it suggests specific models from mics you've starred, with a one-tap add.

Gear Scout now remembers who is selling each new Reverb and eBay ad. When a seller has 2+ other ads, the card shows a '🏪 N other ads' tag (likely a dealer or flipper, often open to bundle deals). It fills in as new ads arrive.

title: Mic searches run every 15 minutes again
items: The 15-minute mic search was taking about 19 minutes, so every other round got skipped. Craigslist searches that found nothing were each launching a slow browser; they now finish instantly. Canadian stores are no longer searched, and a couple of mics are searched at once.
A full round of mic searches should now take a few minutes instead of 19.

title: Gear Scout improves itself every hour
items: An hourly update now ships one improvement at a time on its own: new capabilities, sharper matching and better prices. Each is tested, and undone automatically if anything breaks.
Proposals became 'Coming next' on Home. They're built without waiting for you. Tap Skip on any you don't want, or 'Do this first' to move one up.
Updates never restart Gear Scout in the middle of a 15-minute sweep any more.

title: Only real deals in your updates
items: United and Dachman mics still all show in their own sections, but they reach your updates, Mic deals, pushes and the morning email only when they're in your price range AND at least 20% under their used value. Before, a $899 UT FET47 (its normal used price) and a Dachman priced over used got in.

title: Deal checks, offers, proposals and a morning email
items: Scam check: deals with warning signs (a 'brand new, several available' ad, Zelle or wire requests, contact off the site, shipping only, a photo reused on another ad, a local ad far below market) aren't pushed. They sit under a ⚠️ line or in 'Check these'.
Photo check: the AI looks at each deal's photo and says whether it shows the item in the title. A wrong photo, or a catalogue photo on a local ad, counts as a warning.
Best deals are sorted by a deal score: the discount, plus a little for a fresh ad, a price cut or pickup within 150 miles.
Offer helper: ads whose price was cut, or that have sat 3+ weeks, show a suggested offer (about 15% under) with a Copy message button.
eBay auctions show the most to bid to stay 50% under the used value.

Real sold prices: Gear Scout now records Reverb listings that truly sold, not just ended. Once a model has 3+ sales, its used value comes from those. Reverb closed its public price history, so this builds up over the coming weeks.
A morning email at 8 AM with today's best deals, and a Proposals section on Home: a new idea each night, with Build or Skip.

title: New home page and honest used prices
items: The Home page (was Mics) now opens with what's new since your last visit, then the best deals on everything on your Telex List posted in the last 150 days, then your mics.

Used values are rebuilt: the middle of what single, used US listings of that exact model asked over the last year, with 3 or more needed. An audit found about a quarter of the old values were off by 50% or more: Telex prices or new prices counted as 'used', pairs priced as one, and vintage, reissue and FET versions lumped together.
Every mic brand except United and Dachman now shows, and pushes, only at 50% or more under its used value, and $300 or more. United, Dachman and the Distressor keep their price ranges.
Mics with too few listings to judge, or more than 75% under (usually a scam), are in a closed 'Check these' section at the bottom. They don't push.

title: Faster clicks
items: Search and the Mics page no longer freeze for several seconds (sometimes minutes). Gear Scout's price-history refresh, every 15 minutes, now runs on its own, out of the page's way.

title: Reverb was blocking Gear Scout — fixed
items: Found that Reverb's security layer (Cloudflare) had started turning away Gear Scout's Python requests: the every-2-hours mic read failed every time since yesterday, and Reverb sold checks and price lookups were being blocked too.

Gear Scout now falls back to curl (which Reverb lets through) whenever that happens, for Reverb searches, sold checks, price lookups and shipping reads. Tested live: searches and sold checks work again.
Code review: the AI "Is this a good deal?" check also reads a Reverb ad's full text through that fallback now, so it no longer falls back to the short saved description.
New ads still reach you fast (half within 20 minutes). Your non-mic Wanted terms still show as days old because Mic Focus is on. AudioKarma is still blocked.

title: Sold Reverb ads come down faster
items: Found that a sold SSL Big Six stayed in your Feed for about a day: most of the Feed's Reverb ads were going 4+ hours (some 24+) without a sold check because the hourly check ran out of room.
Reverb ads now get their own allowance of up to 250 checks an hour (Reverb has no daily limit), so sold ones should drop off within a few hours.
New ads still reach you fast: half within 40 minutes, 25 of 32 within an hour. AudioKarma is still blocking Gear Scout, nothing else is failing.

title: Code review
items: A Distressor pair listed as '$1,300 each' was counted as $1,300 total and could show as a deal under the $2,400 pair limit; it now counts as $2,600.
The every-2-hours deep Reverb mic read now also clears a wrong 'sold' mark on a mic that is still listed.

title: Nightly check: all quiet
items: Checked the top 40 Feed ads: 35 still for sale, 1 sold on Reverb (the hourly sold check will remove it), 4 Facebook ads not opened.
New ads reach you fast: half within 30 minutes, 21 of 23 within an hour. No errors in the logs, so nothing was changed tonight.
Your non-mic Wanted terms haven't been searched for about 37 hours because Mic Focus is on. Turn it off if you want everything searched again.

title: Empirical Labs Distressor deals
items: New Mics section: Empirical Labs Distressor (EL8, EL8-X and so on). A deal is a single at $1,300 or less, delivered, or a pair at $2,400 or less. A listing sold as a pair or '2x' counts against the pair price, and the card shows it as '$2,400 for 2 ($1,200 each)'. You get a push and an email for each, and auctions count too.
Brochures, manuals, knobs and software are left out, and so are Distressor clones and 'style' copies.

title: Frozen routines can't hide anymore
items: If the nightly update or the code review hasn't finished in 30 hours (it's usually frozen on an approval prompt nobody can see), Gear Scout now pushes and emails you, at most once a day, with the exact steps to unfreeze it. It checks every 3 hours.

Fixed the cause of the Oct 28 freeze: the instructions for both routines told them to copy the code into a scratch folder with `cp`, and that command asks for approval. They now `docker cp` straight into the container instead.

title: Nightly check: newest mics really on top
items: 'In your price range' now goes by when the seller posted the ad, not when Gear Scout first found it. Newly added brands (and the new deeper Reverb read) turn up old dealer ads, some listed since 2017, which had pushed this week's ads down the list.
Spot check of 40 price-range mics: all real mics in the right section and all 40 still for sale (5 Facebook ads opened). Most new ads were found within an hour of being posted.
Car amplifiers sold as 'SSL EVO' or 'SSL Evolution' (Sound Storm, not Solid State Logic) no longer match your 'ssl' term. There were 20 of them.
While Mic Focus is on, your other Telex terms aren't searched (Health shows them 13+ hours old). That's how Mic Focus works; turn it off on the Mics page when you want the full Telex search back.

title: Mics: older Reverb ads, titles without 'microphone', and email
items: Gear Scout was reading only the newest 150 results of each Reverb search, so for brands with hundreds of used listings (Neumann, AKG) the older ads that were still for sale were never seen. Every 2 hours each brand search is now read 500 results deep. The first read found 312 mics Gear Scout didn't have (298 older ads, 14 new ones, including a $399 Dachman DA87). Older ads are stored but not pushed.
Searches for brands like 'dachman microphone' used to need the word 'microphone' in the listing title, so 'Dachman DA87' or 'Neumann U87 Ai' were dropped. The title now only has to name the brand.
Mic alerts now also come by email (one email per batch of new mics, with pictures, prices and links), not just a push. The email goes to the same address as your digest.

title: Code review
items: The eight new mic brands (Telefunken, Mojave, Soyuz, Josephson, Flea, JZ, Neumann, AKG) only counted an ad when its title had a model number. 'Telefunken Tube Recording Microphone', 'Josephson C551FA Microphone' or a Soyuz 013 FET were left out. Fixed: about 18 more mics now show in 'In your price range' and about 120 more in the brand sections. Mic preamps ('V76 Mic Pre'), direct boxes and loose spare tubes from those brands stay out.

title: Mics page: lowest price per model, in order
items: Each mic section now opens with a 'Lowest price per model' table: every model, its cheapest listing (tap to open) and how many are for sale, cheapest first.
The cheapest ad of each model is highlighted on its card (💲 Lowest, with a colored border) in its section and in 'In your price range'.
The cards in each section are in the order of the price they show. They used to be sorted by price per piece, so a $1,299 pair showed up before a $650 single.
Listings priced under 20% of what that model sells for are left out. They're scams, fakes or parts, like a 'Neumann U87' for $100. Spare nuvistor tubes (13CW4 and similar) are left out too.
Lauten's minimum is now $150.
Every Lauten from $150 up to your limit shows again, including the LA-120, LA-220 and the Tom, Snare and Kick mics. Only Lautens over the limit stay hidden.

title: Eight more mic brands
items: New sections on the Mics page: Telefunken, Mojave, Soyuz, Josephson, Flea and JZ ($300 to $1,000, like the rest), plus Neumann and AKG, which only show and push when one is 30%+ under what that model sells for used (otherwise they'd flood the page with TLM 103s and C414s at normal prices).

Each brand's non-mic products and clones are left out: Neumann monitors and headphones, Telefunken radios and TVs, AKG headphones and wireless, Soyuz's Launcher DI, 'Soviet clone AKG' and '-style' copies, flea markets and the Chili Peppers bassist's gear. AKG D12s stay in their own section.

title: Nightly check: sold mics drop off sooner
items: The hourly sold check now looks at your Mics page's 'In your price range' list first, then the rest of the Mics page. Before, it went through about 400 Feed ads first, so about half of your price-range mics went 5 to 19 hours between checks.

Spot check of 40 price-range mics: all were real mics in the right section, and 38 were still for sale. A Peluso TR-14 (Reverb) and a Serrano Vintage 87 (Craigslist) had just sold. The next hourly check removes them.

Mic searches are on time: every 15 minutes on Reverb, Craigslist and the other fast sites, eBay within half an hour, and each Facebook brand search within 10 hours. Most new ads were found within an hour of being posted.
AudioKarma now blocks Gear Scout. Health shows it as a 'feed parse error', but it's a block. Nothing to do; it was rarely finding anything.

title: Code review
items: Lowest Price trackers leave out overseas eBay sellers, like the rest of Gear Scout. Their eBay 'cheapest first' search was letting UK, Korean and Chinese sellers in (12 of 38 results for 'neve 1073'), so one could have been pushed as a new lowest.
When Facebook asks Gear Scout to slow down, the four daily full scrapes, 'Scrape now' and the favorites price check now leave Facebook alone too, like everything else already did.

title: Code review
items: Mic Focus really pauses Telex List pushes now. The hourly refresh was still sending new Telex matches to your phone (about 20 in the last day), and the end-of-run lowest-price check was still running for Telex terms.
Mic auctions follow the WA-14's own $300 limit. A WA-14 auction at $350 would have been listed and pushed, showing 'your limit $900'.
Deals and Steals in Mic Focus are US-only, like the Mics page. Two Canadian mics (a Kijiji D12 VR and a Canadian Reverb United 87) are gone from Deals.
Rolls and Vanguard mixers ('Mic/Source Mixer', 'Sound Mixer') are no longer counted as mics.
Saving the Mics page settings (on/off, limits) updates Deals and Steals right away. Before, they could take up to 10 minutes.

title: Fewer Lauten mics; Warm Audio narrowed
items: Lauten now shows only their studio mics (Eden, Atlantis, Clarion, Oceanus, Horizon, Torch, the LA-320 tube) at or under your Lauten limit. Their LA-120 / LA-220 budget mics and Tom, Snare and Kick drum mics are left out, and so is anything over the limit.
Warm Audio is now just the WA-CX12 (and the stereo pair), the Fentone and the WA-14 (and WA-14 SP pair), from $150 to $900. Other Warm mics aren't shown or searched.
Other Warm Audio mics (WA-251, WA-47 and so on) no longer turn up in the U47 / 251-style or C12 groups either. Brands with their own section stay in it.
WA-14s only show up to $300, and Warm's minimum is $150.

Mics page: an ad you hide with the ✕ stays gone. Before, it came back on the next reload until the list was rebuilt. Hiding one also hides its re-posts (same title and price), and ads that sell or go pending drop off as soon as Gear Scout knows.

New on the Mics page: Vanguard Audio Labs (V13, V44S, V1S, V4 and others), $300 to $1,000, searched as 'vanguard microphone', 'vanguard v13' and 'vanguard audio labs'. Vanguard tripods and bags are left out.

title: Mics page refreshes itself; Facebook checks each brand more often
items: An open Mics page checks every minute for a finished sweep and reloads itself, so it no longer sits on what was there when you opened it. It also checks when you come back to the tab, and never reloads while you're typing in the settings.

Facebook now runs one broad search per mic brand (17 searches instead of about 45), so each brand gets searched there about every 2 hours during the day instead of every 5 to 14, at the same load on the account. Reverb, eBay, Craigslist and the other fast sites still run every mic search every 15 minutes.

Older mic ads found before Oct 7 (when Gear Scout started noting when it last saw an ad) are back on the Mics page, about 200 of them, like a $399 WA-47 on Facebook. They don't push. The hourly sold check now looks at the Mics page first, your price range first, so the ones that have sold drop off within a few hours.

Cheap WA-47s now show as deals. Gear Scout had been reading 'WA-47 Jr' (the cheaper FET mic) as the WA-47 tube, so hiding Jr ads counted as disputing the tube WA-47's price, and no WA-47 could be a deal. The same thing happened to the AKG D12 with 'D12-type' knockoffs. Fixed, and both disputes cleared: a $300 WA-47 is 45% under the ~$548 they sell for.
In Mic Focus, the Deals and Steals pages cover your mic list (not the paused Telex List): about 150 mic deals right now. Attenuator pads and aviation headsets are left out.
Warm Audio mics over $500 aren't shown anywhere now (Mics page, Warm section, Deals), and Warm pushes stay at $300–$500. Every price limit now includes the limit itself ($500 counts as under $500).

🔨 eBay auctions for your mics: each mic is searched on eBay auctions every hour, and the Mics page lists ones ending in the next 3 days with bid + shipping under your limit. About an hour before one ends you get a push if it's still under (the bid is re-checked with eBay first).
📱 Mercari alerts: Mercari blocks Gear Scout, so the Mics page has a checklist of your 17 mic searches. Open each in the Mercari app, tap Save this search, and Mercari pushes new ones to you.
The catch-all (47 / 67 / 87 / 251 / C12) no longer picks up brands that have their own section (a Warm WA-87 FET isn't a Warm tube mic), handheld or dynamic mics, wireless, Bluetooth or earbuds.

title: Nightly check back on, safer saving, scanners off your Feed
items: The nightly check and the code review had been stuck since Oct 20, waiting for a permission click nobody saw. They're unstuck and will run again tonight. Gear Scout itself kept finding ads the whole time.

Changing your Telex List or Settings now saves in one step. Before, the file sat empty for a split second, and a page that read it at that moment broke (it happened once today, when you removed a term).
NASCAR scanner radios ("RE1000") and Voltech power analyzers ("PM1000") are filtered out. Your Re1000 and Pm1000 terms still find the mic and the Yamaha console.
Spot check of 40 Feed ads: all still for sale. New ads reached you within about 20 minutes (20 of 25 within an hour).
Health now marks the connector part numbers that are searched on Facebook every 3 days, so their older times don't look like a problem.
Still your call: two Calrec consoles list "SSL modules" in their titles and show under "ssl". That's the same question as SSL-style gear from Oct 20.

title: Mic Focus: Gear Scout hunts only your mics now
items: New 🎤 Mics page, now the front page. It covers Peluso, Golden Age tube mics, Stam tube mics, Warm Audio tube mics, Lauten, Bees Neez tube mics, Advanced Audio, United Studio Technologies, Signal Art, Dachman Audio, the AKG D12, C12-style tube mics, and U47 / ELA M 251-style tube mics.

Every 15 minutes Gear Scout searches just those mics: the fast sites every time, eBay every 30 minutes, and Facebook in rotation. Any one under its price goes to your phone, once per price (a price drop sends it again).

Prices are delivered (with listed shipping): from $300 (cheaper ones are usually parts or lookalikes) up to under $1,000 for each mic, under $375 for C12-style tube mics and under $500 for the AKG D12. You can change any of them on the Mics page. Each card also shows how far under the new price it is (or the used price, for mics no longer made). US listings only; spare tubes, capsules, parts, power supplies, repair jobs and multi-mic lots are left out.

Everything else is paused while Mic Focus is on: Telex List matches, steals, price drops, auctions and the AI briefing. Your Telex List is kept. Turn Mic Focus off on the Mics page to go back. The other pages are under More.
Each mic now shows every listing still for sale from the last 90 days, lowest price first, open on the page. Pushes are still only for ones a site showed in the last 10 days.
Dachman: listings that just say 'DA 87SE', 'DA-87i', 'DA FET 47' or 'DA 67' now count as Dachman (unless another brand is named), and 'DA 87SE' is searched too.

New catch-all: 'Any 47 / 67 / 87 / 251 / C12 mic' picks up mics sold by model number alone, from any brand or none ('47 tube mic', 'U87 clone', 'Vintage 87', 'TC-67'), searched as '47 microphone', '67 microphone' and so on. Mics from your named brands stay in their own sections.

title: Vintage King is back, and Facebook searches your mics more often
items: Vintage King had been failing for about 2 weeks because their site moved to a new shop system. Gear Scout reads the new one now: about 180 used and demo items in stock, including 4 on your Wanted list you hadn't seen (SSL Origin console, SSL 2+, Soyuz Silver 17, Mojave MA-37). Some may show up as new on your Feed.

Facebook: the connector part numbers (Neutrik NC3FXX, Hosa DTP-805 and so on) almost never turn up there, so they're searched on Facebook every 3 days instead. Your mic and outboard terms get those turns. Facebook load stays the same.
Spot check of the top 40 Feed ads: all 40 still for sale, 39 were real matches, and new ads reached you within about 20 minutes (26 of 27 within an hour).

Your call: the "ssl" term also catches SSL-style gear (Warm Audio and Tegler bus compressors, and a Soundcraft console with "SSL style modules"). Do you want those? If not, they can be dropped. Stam and Audioscape ones would still show under those terms.

title: Code review
items: Inbox: ✓ Done now really clears an ad — a steal you marked done no longer pops back under “New since you last looked”. A further price cut or an auction about to end still shows.
All-ads page: the All, Newest first and “show all terms” buttons stay on the full list instead of jumping back to the inbox.

Price Board: between its 6-hourly Facebook checks, the Facebook ads it already found stay in the top 10, so the lowest price no longer jumps around and you won't get a “new lowest” alert for an ad that's pricier than a Facebook one.
Price Board and saved searches leave Facebook alone 1–7 AM and while Facebook has asked the account to slow down.

title: Follow-ups from the Oct 18 code review
items: Gentler on Facebook: the Price Board's “still for sale?” check now opens only each term's single cheapest Facebook ad (about 20, not up to 72), at most every 6 hours, and never 1–7 AM.
A Trek bike and a rack shelf that matched “ssl” are filtered out.
Saved slides: the cover counts pieces of gear (a pair is 2), and the running-total chart stays readable if an early buy cost more than new.

title: Flower postcards off your Feed
items: eBay postcards like “Flowerpower No.1 Tulips Art Unlimited Amsterdam Holland Postcard P16” were matching your “ART P16” term (the publisher is Art Unlimited, the card number is P16). Postcards, greeting cards, art prints, posters, lithographs and flowers are now filtered out everywhere, the same way tractors and T-shirts already are.
Checked against your whole Feed: no real gear is affected.

title: New: 🎸 Sweetwater used-gear sweep
items: Sweetwater's used gear (Gear Exchange) blocks automated browsers with a “press & hold” human check, so Gear Scout can't search it on its own.
The new Sweetwater page walks your Telex terms one at a time and opens each search in a Sweetwater tab in your own browser: automatically every 15–90 seconds, or with Next and Back.
Mark each term “Found something” (with an optional note like a price) or “Nothing”. Gear Scout remembers, and starts the next pass with the terms you checked longest ago.

Sweetwater page: a one-time setup checklist for automatic alerts. 25 saved searches (Sweetwater's limit) that cover 56 of your 84 Telex terms. Each has a one-tap link; save it on Sweetwater, turn on the bell, tick it off here.

title: Emails: the fix is yours to finish, plus a safer sign-in
items: Why emails stopped: the saved email password isn't a Gmail app password (those are always 16 letters). Gmail refuses anything else from Gear Scout. Make one at myaccount.google.com/apppasswords (2-Step Verification needs to be on) and paste it in Settings → Email. Google shows it with spaces; Gear Scout removes them.

Gear Scout's sign-in has its own password now. Before, logging in used the same field as the email app password, so a new app password would have changed your login, and the sign-in page (reachable through your phone link) guarded your Gmail credential. Your sign-in password stays exactly what it is today; change it any time in Settings → Email.
Settings warns if a pasted email password doesn't look like an app password.
Inbox: hiding a card with ✕ now removes the whole card, including its ✓ Done button.

Deals and Steals pages weren't empty, just filtered: Deals opened on “posted in the last 3 days, $500–$2,000” (none right now, out of 99 deals), and Steals only counted ones posted this week. Deals now opens on every deal, newest first, with the filters still there. Steals counts everything in its headline and shows the older and double-check ones right away when nothing new was posted this week.

title: Gentler on Facebook, so Marketplace search stops getting paused
items: Facebook pauses Marketplace search on an account that searches constantly. Gear Scout was running about 95–115 Facebook searches an hour, around the clock. It's now about 40 an hour in the daytime and none overnight.

Price Board trackers (api 550, audioscape) were searching every Facebook region every 30 minutes. They now include Facebook every 6 hours; the other sites are still every 30 minutes, and your Telex sweep covers Facebook in between. A check you start yourself always includes Facebook.
1–7 AM Pacific: no background Marketplace searching or feed reading. Groups, posts and anything you start yourself carry on. (Change or turn off with facebook_quiet_hours in config.yaml.)
One-term searches load one Facebook page at a time instead of two at once.
Your Telex terms are still searched on Facebook 2 at a time every 30 minutes in the daytime, so new Marketplace ads reach you as quickly as before.

title: New front page: your inbox
items: The front page is now an inbox of only what needs your attention: auctions ending in the next 48 hours, steals, price cuts of 10%+ in the last 3 days, changes on gear you starred, and new ads since you last looked.
Tap “✓ Done” on a card (or “✓ All done” on a section) and it leaves the inbox for good. The ad itself stays on the Telex List.
Every ad for a term still lives on the Telex List. “All N ads” on the inbox shows the old full list.
Telex List: each term's listings start collapsed. Tap “Show N listings”, or “Expand all terms” at the top.
The search bar now has black text on a light field so it's easy to read.

Market analytics at the bottom of the inbox, for every Telex term: whether prices are falling or rising (last 2 weeks vs the 4 before, with a 6-week mini chart), how fast it sells, how many sell within a week, how many are for sale and the cheapest, new ads per week, how often sellers cut prices, how long ads sit, and a one-line buying tip. Leaderboards on top: prices falling, prices rising, sells fastest, best to haggle, most for sale. Updated hourly.

title: Nightly: cleaner Feed, and your emails need a look
items: Two forestry tillers ($42,500 and $85,419, model “SSL-175”) were showing on your Feed under “ssl”. Forestry and tiller ads are now filtered out.

Your “XLR cable” and snake terms no longer bring up microphones, mixers and recorders that just come “with XLR cable” (Shure SM58s, a Zoom H4n, a Mackie mixer bundle…). Real cables, snakes, patchbays, wall plates and connector lots still show.
Checked the top 40 Feed ads by hand: every one I could open was still for sale, and new ads reach you fast (half within 20 minutes of being posted).

Please look: Gear Scout's emails (daily digest and email alerts) haven't gone out since Oct 15. Gmail closes the connection when Gear Scout tries to send. Phone alerts still work. Check that Gmail hasn't flagged the account, or make a new app password and put it in Settings. The Health page now shows whether emails are going out.
Facebook has paused Marketplace search on your account again (until about 4:30 pm today). Your groups are still searched in the meantime.

title: Code review: about 80 missing Wanted ads are back
items: Since Oct 7, a check meant to keep junk out of broad terms was also hiding real gear: “SSL Big Six”, “SSL Fusion”, “SSL AWS 948”, Peluso, Audioscape, Stam Audio, BeesNeez, Sebatron, Warm Audio WA-19 and Golden Age GA-47 listings never reached your Feed, alerts or Price Board. About 80 of them are back; pianos, comics and paintings that share those names stay out.

Picking a term on the Feed and then Deals or Steals now shows only deals or steals. Before, every model's cheapest ad was pinned on top whether it was a deal or not (for “ssl” + Steals, about 48 ads instead of 1).
The Price Board's full hourly refresh runs on time again. Quick fixes to a few rows (when a cheapest ad sells) kept pushing it back; overnight it went about 4 hours without one.
Saved page: names like “NS10s” or “C414s” count as a pair and are looked up as NS10 / C414.

title: Saved: more pieces priced
items: “beyer 818” searches as Beyerdynamic M818, so shorthand Beyer mic names find their listings.

Listings Gear Scout finds that say “brand new”, “new in box” or “sealed” now count toward a piece's new price. That helps with gear sold mainly direct by its maker. A private “brand new” ad priced under the used market average is treated as a bargain, not as what new costs.
When no new price can be found, the page and slides now say “no new price found” instead of claiming the gear isn't sold new.

title: Saved: pairs and active/passive priced right
items: A plural name (“mixcubes”, “NS10s”, “mics”) counts as a pair, like “x 2” does.
Listings for a pair now count, priced per piece ($300 a pair = $150 each). Before, every “pair” listing was ignored as a lot.
“Active” gear is never priced off passive versions (and the other way round). Your active MixCubes pair at $200 is now $100 under the used market, not $30 over.
A row with two things in it (“4 x CAPI VP28 / 4 x …”) prices each part and adds them up. CAPI “VM28” is read as the VP28.

title: Saved: vs new, vs the used market, and where you overpaid
items: Every piece now gets two prices: today's new price (Reverb Brand New + eBay New) and its used market average (your Telex prices, then listings Gear Scout has found, then Reverb).
“Saved” is always against new. Gear that isn't made new any more is compared to its used market average and says so: never labeled “new”.
New Analytics on the Saved page: 1) saved vs new, 2) saved vs the used market average, 3) where you overpaid, plus best buys, what your gear is worth used today, and prices worth double-checking.
Slides show NEW, USED MARKET AVERAGE and YOU PAID bars on every piece, and a new “Market check” slide.
Junk new listings (cables and parts that mention the same model) no longer drag a new price down, and your Telex term names help find the right gear (“vanguard 13” searches as “Vanguard V13”).

title: Gear Scout has its brand back
items: The whole app now wears the original Gear Scout look, the same as the Saved page's social slides: the knob, VU meter and patch-cable logo, the “Gear Scout” wordmark, charcoal top bar with an orange edge, warm paper pages and Fraunces italic headings.
The home-screen icon is the new logo too (remove and re-add Gear Scout to your home screen if your phone keeps the old one).

title: Saved: every piece gets a real price
items: Items without a new price now use today's going used price: your Telex List prices first, then listings Gear Scout has found, then Reverb. Before, discontinued or shorthand items (260VU, Ampex, Sony 56s, Distressors…) counted as $0 saved.
Quantities count: “x 2”, “(2)”, “pair” or “20's” multiply the price.
Brand-last names work (“la-2a audioscape”), plurals work (“distressors”), and parts, cards, cabinets and add-ons no longer drag a price down (the Ampex 440C was being priced off $150 preamp cards).
A piece you paid over today's price stays in the table but is left off the social slides.

title: Saved slides wear the Gear Scout brand
items: The social slides now use the original Gear Scout logo (knob, VU meter and patch-cable mark) and wordmark, in charcoal, cream and orange with the Fraunces italic and IBM Plex type.
The cover reads “You saved $X using Gear Scout”, and each piece shows “You saved” and “You paid”.
The fonts are built into each slide, so the PNGs you save look exactly like the preview on any phone.

title: New: 💰 Saved page with social slides
items: Paste a Google Sheet link (columns Item and Paid; New, Date and Where optional) and Gear Scout shows what you saved on each piece vs. buying new, plus a running total.
Rows without a new price get today's Reverb “Brand New” price automatically.
Makes 1080×1080 slides for Instagram/Facebook: a cover with your total, one slide per piece, a leaderboard and a running-total chart. Save one or all as images.

title: Lowest price picks: older ads count again
items: Fixed: some of your cheapest ads were never marked “💲 Lowest” because the parts filter read brand names as parts. “sE Electronics” looked like “electronics (part)”, and “w/ gold XLR connector” looked like a loose connector. The VR2 Voodoo now shows the $349 ad from 2024 instead of a $375 one.
Fixed: “HEDD Type 20” was treated as a knock-off (“type”), and “Audioscape … SSL style” was skipped as a copy even though that’s exactly what the term asks for. Both now get their cheapest marked.
Connector terms (Neutrik NP3X, NC3MXX…) now count connector listings.

title: Cables, snakes and patchbays on your list
items: ✕ on an ad now hides it for good: it stays hidden after the 90-day cleanup, and a repost of the same ad (new link, same title and price on Facebook or Craigslist) is hidden too, with no push or email. The 294 ads you'd already hidden are remembered. Settings → Unhide all still brings everything back.

Terms that are cables, snakes, patchbays or connectors (“XLR snake”, “Hosa DTP-805”, “Neutrik NC3FXX”, “Canare L-4E6S”) now find those listings — before, they were skipped as accessories, and broad ones were held to a $150 minimum.
You can leave words out of a term with a minus: “patchbay -behringer” finds any patchbay except Behringer.
Added for the studio wiring: Hosa DTP-805, Hosa STX-807F, ART P16, XLR snake, TRS snake, DB25 TRS, patchbay -behringer.

title: Overseas ads removed
items: Steals are back: a steal is now 50%+ under (was 60%), from your Telex List. Ones with only one price to compare against show too, tagged “🔎 Steal? double-check” (up to 90% under) — and steal alerts mark them the same way. Parts like console faders and “box only”, and camcorders, are filtered.

Overseas listings are left out completely: only sellers in the US and Canada. Reverb sellers are identified by the currency they list in (a Japanese shop lists in yen, a UK shop in pounds — about half of Reverb's used Neumann listings were overseas); eBay by the item's location.
They're dropped when scraped and kept out of the Feed, Telex page, Price Board, cheapest picks, deals, alerts and the digest. Listings already stored were checked once.

title: Shipping counts in the cheapest price
items: Fixed: deleting (or adding) several Telex terms one after another no longer stalls the site — the Price Board is rebuilt once, shortly after your last change, and the Telex page and Feed show right away (removed terms gone) while they refresh in the background.

When a site lists shipping, the price you see on every ad is now the delivered price (price + shipping), with the breakdown underneath; free shipping and local pickup are labelled. Cheapest picks, Cheapest first, the Price Board and the Deals page's cheapest sort all go by delivered cost. The digest email and auction / price-drop alerts show shipping too.

Gear Scout now records US shipping for Reverb and eBay listings (to your zip for eBay) and shows it on each card: “free shipping”, “+ $72 shipping · $1,706 delivered”, or “local pickup” for Facebook, Craigslist, OfferUp and Kijiji.

The cheapest per term and per model, “Cheapest first” and the Price Board all decide by price + known shipping (split per piece for pairs and lots). Where a site doesn't show shipping (dealers, ShopGoodwill), it counts as unknown.
Listings already stored are getting their shipping looked up once; it's refreshed whenever a listing is re-checked.

title: Fewer wrong matches for broad terms; Price Board cheapest fixed
items: “Cheapest first” (Telex page, and now also on the Feed) includes every ad still for sale whatever its age — it used to sort only the last week and leave older, cheaper ads in the collapsed section.

Models are recognised however they're written: “VT-737SP”, “VT 737 sp”, “737sp” and “VT-737” are all one Avalon 737; Distressors split cleanly into EL8 / EL8X / EL8XS. The cheapest of each model is worked out from the list you're looking at (so a new cheaper ad is marked right away), and it no longer skips cheap real units (e.g. the $499 PCM60). Display parts, plug-in bundles, grills, shirts and records filtered.

The cheapest per term and per model is now the cheapest working ad still for sale no matter how old it is (it was limited to ads posted in the last 90 days) — e.g. Daking's cheapest is now a $599 mic pre posted 5 months ago.

For terms that cover several models (“d12” → D12, D12E, D12VR; “Lexicon pcm” → PCM60, PCM70, PCM91…), the cheapest working one of EACH model now comes first, cheapest model first, with a gold “💲 Lowest <model>” tag. The term's overall cheapest still pulses. Each is checked to still be for sale; add-on cards, ROMs, manuals and copies don't count.

Every term now gets a “cheapest anywhere”, brands too (daking, stam, peluso, beesneez…), from any working ad still for sale posted in the last 90 days. Furniture is filtered out (“Mart Stam” dining chairs).

Filtered out off-topic listings that share letters with your terms: tractors and loaders (“SSL attach”), trailers, mowers, guitar pickups (Seymour Duncan SSL-1…), guitars by model (Strat, Tele, Les Paul…), T-shirts and jerseys — about 130 removed.

Fixed the site hanging: “Scrape now” runs as its own lower-priority process (it used to share the website's process and starve the pages), the Feed shows the current list instantly and refreshes in the background after any change, and a saved copy makes it load instantly after a restart. A Scrape now cut off by a restart no longer stays “running” forever (which also paused the hourly refresh).

The cheapest working listing for each term (the Price Board's “cheapest anywhere”) now pulses gold with a “💲 Lowest” tag, and sits at the top of that term on the Telex page and when you filter the Feed by a term. Broken / “Non Functioning” ads no longer count as the cheapest.

Each term's cheapest is checked to still be for sale (re-checked if not confirmed in the last 3 hours; if it's gone, the next cheapest takes over) and can be any ad posted in the last 90 days. The Feed now keeps ads up to 90 days old that are still listed.
Broad terms (“DIY”, “Golden age”) and short model codes without a brand (“se8”) now only match listings that look like audio gear — no more tiny homes, die-cast cars, Batman art or network switches.
Records, albums and CDs named like gear (“Whirr – Distressor” LP) are filtered out; the PRS Mary Cries is recognised as a pedal.
Price Board “cheapest anywhere” skips junk priced far under what the model normally asks, and skips clones / “style” / “type” copies unless your term asks for a clone.
Tip: for the real thing only, name the maker — “Teletronix LA-2A” or “UA LA-2A” instead of “LA-2A” (which also finds AudioScape and other copies).
Fixed: adding a term didn't update its Price Board row until the next hourly rebuild.

title: Code review fixes
items: Telex page shows every new ad on your list, at any price (it only showed ones 10%+ under their usual price — about two-thirds of new ads never appeared there: 31 shown vs. 126 posted in the last 2 days). It now uses the same listings as the Feed, newest first, deals marked.
Scrape now (also on the Feed) re-reads every site and then searches every one of your terms; it reports how many new ads are on your list. It no longer deletes listings older than 30 days.
Listings are cleaned up by when a site last showed them, not when they were first found — long-running ads no longer come back as “new”, and ones still listed stay on the Feed.
Price increases are shown; an ad wrongly marked sold comes back when a site shows it again; “✓ still listed” only appears when a check actually confirmed it.

Fresher searches: Reverb and Kijiji term searches now sort newest first (they used “best match”), specific models are searched on all of eBay (not just Pro Audio), and Facebook's hourly refresh adds a newest-first search in every region.
Adding a term on the Telex page searches it right away; the comma-joined Lexicon entry now works everywhere (Price Board, lowest-price alerts).
Phone alerts for a new match now include the listing's photo. Favorites show a pink title, and the ★ Favorites link is pink in the top bar.

One deal calculation everywhere: the Feed's badges and Deals/Steals filters, the digest email, the Price Board, the Deals and Steals pages and the steal alerts now all give a listing the same “% under” (the Feed used to use a different, stricter formula). Steals = 60%+ under everywhere.
Price Board counts the same listings as the Feed (it used to include ads not seen for months), and its “best deal this week” matches the Deals page. It's rebuilt hourly.
Facebook safety: if Facebook asks your account to slow down, every Facebook search (Marketplace, groups, posts, sold checks) now pauses together for a few hours, and you get a push.
Digest email lists deals first; the per-site lines say how many listings were read (not “new”).

title: Everything now follows your Wanted list
items: Auction alerts, the digest email, steal and price-drop alerts, the AI briefing and the Deals/Steals pages now only cover your Telex List — no more irrelevant gear (e.g. this week's auction alerts: 16 random items before, 2 on your list now).
The regular scrapes no longer throw away gear you want: “lexicon 960” now keeps “Lexicon 960L”, “Avalon 737” keeps “VT-737sp”, Eventide H9000s etc. (hundreds a month were being dropped).

Fewer junk matches: “link audio”, “Coil audio” and similar brand terms need the brand name together (no more PS Audio Digital Link or moving-coil phono cartridges); spare tubes with “V72 V76” stuffed in the title are filtered.
Your terms are really searched every 30 minutes now (a timing slip made it hourly), and new matches are pushed before the slower sold check runs.
Telex page explains what the list does and links every term to all its listings on the Feed. The old Dashboard is now “Browse all” (everything collected, not just your list).
“New since you last looked” only shows ads posted in the last 2 weeks; old ads Gear Scout just dug up go to “Older ads”, tagged NEW.

title: New home page: one Feed for your Wanted list
items: 📬 Feed is the new home page: everything for sale that matches your Telex List — at any price, newest post first. The Telex page only showed listings 10%+ under their comp, so normally priced gear never reached you.
“New since you last looked” at the top; anything you've already seen drops below it, so the same listings no longer sit on top day after day.
Only your own Telex List counts now. The imported model group (Cole Picks, e.g. Sony C-38B) and the long keyword list no longer put listings in front of you.

Every Wanted term is now searched directly on Reverb, Craigslist, Kijiji, ShopGoodwill, Long & McQuade and OfferUp every 30 minutes and on eBay every 2 hours (before: each term every 12–40 hours). Facebook Marketplace and group posts rotate through your terms all day.
Phone alert within ~30 minutes for every new ad that matches your Wanted list.

Sold Facebook ads: when a seller deletes or sells an ad, Facebook usually just shows Marketplace with no ad on it — Gear Scout now counts that as gone (about 1 in 5 Facebook ads on your pages were already gone). Feed ads are re-checked first and show when they were last checked.
🩺 Health page: when each term was last searched on each kind of site, how many new ads every site found today, and how fast new ads reach you.
Deals and Steals are now filters on the Feed. The old Dashboard, Deals and Steals pages are still there for now.

title: Nightly update: fewer fake deals, no repeats
items: Rough price estimates can no longer make something look 55–80% off — they mixed in other models (an SSL 1 interface vs. pricier SSL gear, a Lynx Aurora 8 vs. newer Auroras, a Maag PREQ2 vs. pricier Maag modules). Real comparisons are unaffected.

Filtered out: wireless systems that don't say “wireless” (WMS-40, UHF/VHF, bodypacks), car amplifiers (Phoenix Gold), tube testers and test gear, bass trainers/metronomes, mic goosenecks, boom arms described as “… Microphone”, and cables named by length (“HOSA 15 ft XLR to DB25”).
Dashboard: an ad in “Picked for you” no longer repeats in “Deals” right below it.
Brand-only Telex terms (“phoenix audio”, “daking”, “maag”, “overstayer”…) are treated as broad terms: no odds and ends under $150 (a $15 USB conference mic was showing).
Checked: Guitar Center and Sweetwater used gear block automated visits (bot protection), so Gear Scout skips them rather than trying to get around it.
Accuracy check of 60 listings on your pages: ~88% real studio gear and ~87% right comparisons before tonight's fixes (every one still for sale); the junk and misleading estimates found are fixed.

title: Faster term adding, buttons show when they're working
items: Adding a Telex term (the box, the 📋 button on a listing, or Ask AI) now takes a few seconds instead of a minute: only the new term is worked out, and its Price Board row updates in the background. Removing a term is instant.
Any button you press greys out and says “⏳ Working…” until the page comes back, so you know it's doing something.
Scrape and search buttons stay greyed out (“⏳ Running…”) on every page while their job is still running in the background, and come back when it's done.

Much faster overall: the price-history rebuild (every 5 minutes) used to run inside whichever page you opened — up to a minute's wait (Search took 39s). It now runs in the background and is 4–5x faster; Search opens in 2–7s.
Adding or removing a Telex term no longer makes the Dashboard and Deals recalculate everything; Telex opens instantly after an update even if your terms changed.

Much lighter on the Mac: the dashboard no longer redoes all its heavy work every 3 minutes when nothing changed (it now sits near 0% when idle), and the hourly sold check opens 60 Facebook ads instead of 100 (ads on your pages first).

title: Telex List: see what's new
items: New “🆕 New on your Telex List” section at the top: everything posted in the last 2 days across all your terms, newest first, each labeled with its term.
Inside each term, newest posts now come first (one tap for “Cheapest first”), and terms with something new move to the top — the chips show how many are new.
Broad terms (“vintage microphone”, “tube mic”, “stam”…) no longer show odds and ends under $150, and only $300+ finds from them make the New section. Specific models show at any price.

title: Nightly update: alerts fixed, price drops, cleaner deals
items: Fixed: steal alerts were never actually sent (a bug stopped every one). They work now.

New: price-drop alerts — when a seller cuts the price of something in your range and it becomes a real deal (15%+ under what it sells for used), you get a push + email. Sellers who drop their price are usually open to offers too.
New on Deals: “📉 Price just cut” — every deal whose price was lowered in the last week.
Clone makers that name the original (“Stam SA-432D+ Sontec 432D9”, “Stam Pultec MEQP-1A+”) are now priced as the Stam, not the $14,000 original.
Filtered out: loose vacuum tubes (e.g. EC8020 “gold pins”), speaker grilles, voice coils / replacement diaphragms, “(PART)” face plates, mic desk stands and “microphone decor”.
Dashboard “Deals” section keeps to $300–$2,500 (no $25 interfaces); the same ad listed twice shows once on the Telex List.
Accuracy check of 60 listings on your pages: ~88% real studio gear and ~93% right comparisons before tonight's fixes; all junk and wrong comps found are fixed.

title: 📊 Price Board (was Lowest Price)
items: Lowest Price is now a Price Board that fills itself in: one row for every Telex term and tracked item, updated hourly — no typing needed.

Each row shows the best deal posted this week (biggest discount vs. what that gear usually sells for used) and, for specific models, the cheapest one for sale anywhere, plus how many are for sale, how many were posted this week, and whether the lowest price is going up or down.
For brand or category terms (“tube mic”, “stam”), only gear from $300 up — near your $500–$2,000 budget.
New-lowest-price alerts now only fire when the new lowest is also 10%+ under the usual used price.
Ads whose title says SOLD / UNAVAILABLE / “has been sold” are treated as sold everywhere.
The search box for looking up any item and your tracked items are still there, below the board.
Every Scrape / Search button now shows when it last ran and what it found (manual scrape, the hourly automatic refresh, Telex search, live search, price lookup, Facebook post search).
Deals has its own Scrape now button with a progress bar.
Pages stay fast while a scrape runs (they were rebuilding on every progress update).

title: Fresh ads, your budget, Facebook & Craigslist first
items: Facebook Marketplace and Craigslist never say when an ad was posted in their search results — so old ads looked brand new. Gear Scout now reads the real posting date from each ad's own page when it checks whether it sold (no extra requests).
Every listing card shows its age (green = last 2 days, grey = over a week). A “~” means the site doesn't say, so it's when Gear Scout found it.
Fresh means the last week: on the Dashboard, Deals, Steals and every Telex term, ads posted more than a week ago go to a collapsed “older” section.
Facebook Marketplace and Craigslist come first: their sections lead the Dashboard, and on Deals they're first within each day.
Deals opens on the last 3 days and your $500–$2,000 range (one tap for under $500, $2,000+ or any price). “Picked for you” uses the same range and only this week's ads.
Facebook Telex/live searches now ask for the newest ads from the last 30 days; OfferUp term searches are newest-first.
Pages open instantly after an update (Dashboard ~4s, Deals/Steals/Telex under 1.5s instead of 30–80s): the last results are kept on disk and refreshed in the background.

title: Steals: fresh first, scams out
items: Steals now shows newest posts first; ads up 30+ days moved to a section at the bottom.

Scam pattern filtered: several identical ads for the same gear at an impossible price posted within a few days (e.g. four “Genuine Neumann TLM 103” at ~$100) are left out. Anything 80%+ off goes to “Double-check these”.
Plain “Teletronix LA-2A” listings are valued as UA reissues unless they say vintage / original / 1960s.

More parts and accessories caught (option/ADAT cards, shock mount “suspensions”, mic arms, guitar pickups, connectors, “accessory” sets), while gear bundles like “Apollo Twin X, SM7B, M50x, mic arm” are kept.

title: 💸 Deals tab
items: New Deals tab: every listing still for sale that's 10%+ under used prices, newest posts first, with filters for Today / 3 days / This week / This month / Any age.

Ages now come from when the seller posted the ad, not when Gear Scout found it — Gear Scout reads deep into Reverb and eBay, so half of what it finds has been listed 90+ days. Those long-listed ads have their own “Listed 30+ days” filter (good for making offers).
Sort by newest, biggest % off, most dollars saved, or cheapest.
Deals and Steals now share one calculation in the background, so both pages open instantly and the Mac does half the work; this week's newest deals are checked for sold first.
Dashboard: ads the seller posted 30+ days ago moved to their own “Listed 30+ days ago” section at the bottom (biggest discount first), so the top shows fresh finds.
Every manual scrape and search keeps running when you switch pages — and now a small progress bar follows you to every page until it's done (tap it to go back to the results).

title: Auction alerts + search-it-yourself links
items: Auction alerts: every hour Gear Scout checks eBay's pro-audio auctions ending soonest (plus ShopGoodwill). During the day you get a push + email about an hour before a good one ends (current bid 40%+ under the comp).

At 9:30 PM: “Tonight's overnight auctions” — auctions ending between 11 PM and 7 AM with bids 30%+ under value. Fewer people are awake to bid, so set your max bid before bed. Bidding is always up to you.
eBay auctions now show the current bid and end time (they're in the Auctions section on the Dashboard).

Each Telex term now has one-tap “Search it yourself” links: Facebook Marketplace (newest first), eBay sold prices, eBay auctions ending soonest, Reverb, HiBid, LiveAuctioneers, GovDeals, and common misspellings (e.g. “Nueman U47”) on eBay and Marketplace.
Checked auction houses and estate-sale sites for automatic searching: HiBid blocks it, and LiveAuctioneers, AuctionZip and EstateSales.net don't allow it — so they're one-tap links instead.

title: Accuracy check + misspelling search
items: Checked 70 listings from your pages by hand: 81% were real gear before today's fixes; all 13 junk ones in the sample are now filtered (mic pouches, electric guitars, loose speaker woofers, rack trays, spare parts, hi-fi phono cartridges).
UA LA-2A reissues (often titled “Teletronix”) are no longer compared to 1960s originals — the comp drops from about $9,400 to about $4,400.
Price estimates for clones use the clone itself (an Aiwa VM-12 “RCA 77 style” is no longer valued like an RCA).

New: Gear Scout now searches common misspellings of top brands (“Nueman”, “Sennhieser”, “Telefunkin”, “Pulltec”…) a few an hour on eBay, Reverb, Craigslist, OfferUp and others — misspelled ads are found by few buyers and often sell cheap.
Sold listings: every one in the sample had been re-checked within the last few hours, and none were sold.

title: Vintage mics group on the Telex List
items: Added every microphone model Cole Picks Vintage has sold (414 models) to your Telex List as one group, “Vintage mics (Cole Picks sold)”, shown as a single cheapest-first list.
Group models match on brand + exact model number (an RCA 77-DX isn't a 77-D; “Shure 300” doesn't match a $300 price).
Group models are searched about 10 an hour on the fast sites (all covered every couple of days) instead of being added to every scrape, so scrapes stay fast and eBay's daily allowance lasts.
Comps for clones now use the clone itself, not the gear it copies.
The Steals page has a Scrape now button with a progress bar.

title: 🔥 Steals page
items: New Steals page (top menu): everything collected for your terms and Telex List that's 60%+ under used prices (switch to 50/70/80%), biggest dollar savings first.

Every steal is double-checked against what other listings of the same gear ask, so clones, cheaper versions and parts don't show up as fake steals. Shakier ones go in a separate “Double-check these” list.
New steals are pushed to your phone and email within the hour.
Facebook listings you see are now checked for sold status more reliably.

title: AI assistant: deal checks, alerts, briefings
items: Ask AI remembers the conversation — ask follow-ups like “only the ones under $1,000” or “tell me more about #2”.
🤖 button on every listing: the AI reads the full ad, looks at the photo, compares the price with the comp, and gives a verdict, red flags, a fair offer and a ready-to-send message to the seller.

Ask AI can do things for you: add a term to your Telex List, star a listing, run a live search, or set an alert (“tell me when a U47 clone under $800 shows up within 100 miles”). Alerts are checked hourly and sent by push + email.
Daily briefing email at 8 AM: the 5 best finds of the last 24 hours and why.
Weekly market notes on Sundays at 9 AM: what's selling fast, price moves on your Telex gear, and models worth watching.
All of these use your own free Gemini key (Settings → AI); without a key they simply stay off.

title: Sold listings, pedals, new-first, ShopGoodwill
items: Listings on your Dashboard and Telex are re-checked first (every 4 hours) so sold/ended ones drop off; eBay listings are now checked too (through eBay's API).
Guitar pedals are left out everywhere except Search (recognized by type and maker, not just the word 'pedal'), unless one of your terms asks for pedals.
New '🆕 New since your last visit' section at the top of the Dashboard (all sites, newest first) and NEW badges, so you don't see the same top listings every time.
ShopGoodwill: reads the Musical Instruments and Vintage Electronics categories page by page (about 1,000 newest lots per full run) plus deeper searches.
New '🔨 Auctions' section: auctions whose current bid is still 10%+ under the comp, ending soonest first.
The top listings on the Dashboard and Telex are checked for sold/ended right after each page is built (not just hourly), and sold ones are taken off immediately.
New 'Ask AI' page: ask in plain English about the gear Gear Scout has found; Google Gemini (your own free key, Settings → AI) plans the search and answers with links to the listings and their comps.

title: Nightly improvements begin
items: Gear Scout now gets a nightly improvement session (about 1:40 AM): it reviews the day's logs and results, fixes what it finds, adds improvements, and notes them here.
Emails no longer say '⚠️ N source errors' for sites that always block automated access (Guitar Center, Sweetwater, Gearspace) or for eBay pausing at its daily limit — only real failures are flagged.
Facebook sold/pending checks wait only as long as each page needs instead of a fixed 2 seconds, so the hourly check finishes sooner.

Much faster pages: pages are compressed (Dashboard 1.4 MB → ~40 KB), collapsed sections (Show all, No comp yet) load only when you open them, the Dashboard and Telex are kept ready in the background, and starring/hiding no longer forces a rebuild. Dashboard ~0.2s instead of ~5s.

title: B-stock value and 'Worth it only'
items: Each model now gets a B-stock value: what a dealer B-stock / open-box unit goes for (Reverb B-stock listings, or 85% of the new price). Cards show 'B-stock ~$X'.
New 'Worth it only' switch on the Dashboard and search: only listings at least 10% under B-stock value (or under the used value for vintage gear with no B-stock version).
Comps learn from you: hiding a listing Gear Scout called a deal or 'worth it' disputes its comp; after two, the comp is re-checked from scratch and shown as a rough estimate until then.
Sold comps: once Gear Scout has watched a model sell 3+ times, what it actually went for becomes that model's comp ('sold ~$X').
Mixed-price check: if a model's prices are all over the place (vintage and reissue mixed together), its comp isn't trusted for deals or 'worth it'.
Header: navigation has its own row with more space; labels no longer break mid-word.
Telex only shows listings at least 10% under the used price on Reverb (cards show 'Reverb used ~$X · N% under'); ones without a reliable Reverb price are in a collapsed group under each term.
Specific Telex terms ('Avalon 737', 'Distressor', 'Apollo X8P') get their own Reverb price, used for same-brand listings that don't name a model.
Facebook pictures are saved locally while their links work (Facebook links expire), so they keep showing; any picture that still fails shows a clean placeholder.
eBay pauses itself until the daily reset when its daily request allowance is used up; Telex buttons react instantly.

Every Telex listing gets a comp when at all possible: what the model sold for, its Reverb/eBay used price, Gear Scout's own price history (incl. sold listings), the Telex term's price, or similar past listings (est.). The card says which. Listings still without one are looked up first on each hourly refresh.

Dashboard only shows listings at least 10% under their comp (B-stock value when known, otherwise sold / Reverb-eBay used / history / similar listings) — no checkbox; listings without a comp are in one collapsed group at the bottom.

The 10%-under-comp rule applies everywhere: Dashboard, Deals, Telex, FB Posts, the email digests and the Facebook roundup (each listing shows its comp). Search, Lowest Price and favorites still show everything you asked for.
New-lowest-price alerts for every Telex term: a phone push (ntfy) + email when a listing comes in below the lowest price currently listed for that term across all sources.

title: Picked for you = real deals; cleaner Deals
items: Picked for you now only shows gear like your favorites that is 20%+ under a solid market value and within your usual price range (learned from your favorites), best deals first.
Deals need 30%+ under typical (40%+ under Reverb/eBay asking); anything over 85% under is treated as a mismatch, not a deal.
Tubes, tube sets, power supplies, transformers, meter bridges, capsules and other parts are valued as parts and never shown as deals.
Model versions are kept apart: AKG C12 VR vs. vintage C12, C414 XLS vs. XLII, U87 Ai, Mk II, reissues.
Bare model numbers after a brand are recognized (Universal Audio 1176, Neve 1073).
Telex and Lowest Price leave out pedal and plugin versions (UAFX LA-2A pedal, UAD plugins) unless your term asks for them, e.g. 'LA-2A pedal'.

Telex recognizes Universal Audio pedals sold without the word 'pedal' (LA-2A / 1176 'Studio Compressor', Lion '68…) and UA plugin versions of other makers' gear, and leaves out parts, add-ons and anything priced far below what the model sells for.
Telex shows every matching listing still for sale (not just recent ones or the cheapest 60): first 24 on screen, 'Show all' for the rest. Listings are kept 90 days instead of 30.

Air/HVAC compressors (tons, horsepower, R22, Trane, Campbell Hausfeld, Sears…) and consumer speakers (Bluetooth, car audio, PA systems, bookshelf/hi-fi) are filtered out; broad-word matches now need a pro brand or vintage clues, not just a $200+ price.

title: Faster everywhere
items: Reverb now comes through Reverb's data feed instead of a full browser: about 9 seconds instead of 25, and it sees every listing from the last 3 hours instead of just the first page.
Facebook groups are read more briefly on hourly refreshes and stop as soon as there's nothing new.
Dealer stores (Alto, Rudy's, Long & McQuade) are read every 3 hours on hourly refreshes — their stock changes slowly. Full scheduled runs still read them every time.
Market-price lookups run three at a time, and the hourly sold/pending checks run alongside them instead of after — the hourly refresh finishes in about half the time.
Pages open faster: the database got indexes for the lookups every page makes, and the dashboard pre-calculates prices and learning data in the background.
Sold/pending checks run several at a time, with Facebook checked alongside — the hourly check went from about 9 minutes to a couple.

title: Cleaner results, eBay, Telex
items: eBay connected: in scrapes, live search, Lowest Price (cheapest first), market values and Telex searches.
Broad search words (mic, condenser, preamp…) only count when a listing looks like studio gear: a pro brand, vintage clues, or $200+.
Filtered out: toys, karaoke, video games, ham radio, tapes/records, home-stereo gear, wireless mic systems, and accessory-only listings (setting).
Telex: cheapest first, eBay included, 'Search all terms now' and per-term 'Search everywhere' buttons with progress.
Facebook 'Pending' listings tracked and badged; pending items aren't counted as deals.
Dashboard: one section per site with a jump bar; a small site tag on every listing.

title: Smarter comps and learning
items: Comp prices compare like with like: brands recognized anywhere in the title, pedal/plugin/kit/500-series versions valued separately, bundles and parts handled.
Learning: how fast each model sells and what it went for, offer hints on listings up 3+ weeks, and Facebook post search that spends its time on terms that find posts.
